chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Ali ibn Hadeed from Ali ibn Maymun al-Sa'igh, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what is swept up from the dust/soil that I sell, and what I should do with it. He said, 'Give it in charity, for either it is for you or for his family.' I said, 'For indeed it contains gold, silver, and iron, so with what should I sell it?' He said, 'Sell it for food.' I said, 'And if I have a needy relative, should I give it to him from it?' He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling dust containing gold and silver and giving it as charity?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on selling collected dust containing trace minerals, permitting its sale for food to be used as charity (sadaqah) for either the seller or his family. The narration further extends this flexibility to include needy relatives, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of facilitating ease in disposing of minor wealth. This ruling underscores the practical application of purification and charity in daily economic transactions within the Imami tradition.
